body.x: The Seoul Business Agency (SBA, President and CEO Hyun Woo Kim) announced that it has established the Seoul Pavilion at CES 2026, the world’s largest technology exhibition held in Las Vegas, the United States, from Tuesday, January 6 to Friday, January 9 (local time), to support the global market entry of 70 startups.

The Seoul Pavilion is set up within Eureka Park, the startup-focused exhibition area, covering 743 square meters. It consists of a main stage, photo zones, and dedicated consultation spaces for participating companies. Notably, this year marks the first introduction of a media center and an Innovation Award exhibition area within the pavilion to strengthen media promotion for exhibitors and attract more visitors.

The Seoul Pavilion brings together the collective capabilities of Seoul’s startup ecosystem through collaboration among 19 institutions. These include SBA as the lead organization, four district offices of Gangnam-gu, Gwanak-gu, Guro-gu, and Geumcheon-gu, five startup support organizations, including Seoul AI Hub, Seoul Tourism Organization, Seoul Social Venture Hub, Seoul Fintech Lab, and Campus Town Enterprise Growth Center, as well as nine major universities in Seoul: Konkuk University, Kyung Hee University, Kwangwoon University, Sogang University, Seoul National University, Sungkyunkwan University, Yonsei University, Ewha Womans University, and Chung-Ang University.
The 70 companies exhibiting at the Seoul Pavilion span advanced technology sectors such as artificial intelligence, mobility, and healthcare.

Seventy university students selected as student supporters assist with interpretation and overall booth operations for participating companies. The supporters consist of students from the nine major universities in Seoul, along with local Korean students, including those from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, providing comprehensive on-site support for company activities.

On the first day of CES, January 6 (local time), SBA officially launched the four-day exhibition schedule by holding the opening ceremony of the Seoul Pavilion, introducing Seoul’s innovative technologies and city brand to the global audience.

The main concept of the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion opening ceremony was “Seoul POP,” a theme that expressed the explosive moment of Seoul’s condensed innovation and energy through rhythmic visuals, music, and creative performances. The concept symbolized the determination of the 19 participating institutions, 70 companies, and 70 student supporters to unite and showcase Seoul’s technological and innovative energy on the world stage.

During the ceremony, representatives from each participating institution joined on stage to perform using “Seoul POP” can-shaped objects. Startups and student supporters filling the audience lit up cheering sticks in Morning Yellow, Seoul’s color for 2026, further amplifying the excitement at the venue.

body.cap: SBA President and CEO Hyun Woo Kim delivers a welcome address at the CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion opening ceremony. | Provided by the Seoul Business Agency

body.x: During the Seoul POP ceremony, which culminated with a countdown, Kim delivered the message “Seoul Innovators Show Up,” declaring the pavilion open and expressing hope that the Seoul Pavilion would become the most vibrant space at CES and a must-visit destination for global buyers.

In addition to the opening ceremony, SBA operated a variety of on-site programs throughout CES to promote promising Seoul-based companies globally. Just ahead of the CES opening, on January 4, SBA supported the participation of 10 companies, including Innovation Award winners, in the official CES media event “CES Unveiled.”

CES Unveiled is an annual event that offers global media an early preview of selected exhibitors ahead of the official CES opening. Ten outstanding companies from the Seoul Pavilion, including CES 2026 Innovation Award winners, participated in CES Unveiled and drew significant attention from international media outlets.
Backed by these multifaceted support programs, participating startups from the Seoul Pavilion earned 17 Innovation Awards, including one Best of Innovation Award.

To externally validate Seoul startups' innovations and enhance global recognition, SBA provided two months of advanced consulting support for Innovation Award applications. As a result, 17 companies, including one Best of Innovation Award winner, received CES 2026 Innovation Awards.

The CES Innovation Awards are presented annually by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), the organizer of CES, to products and technologies that demonstrate excellence in engineering, design, and innovation.

The Best of Innovation Award was won by STUDIO LAB, a member of SBA’s Innovation Award community, placing it alongside global corporations such as Samsung and Qualcomm. Only about 30 companies worldwide receive the Best of Innovation Award each year.

SBA President and CEO Hyun Woo Kim said, “The CES Seoul Pavilion is not merely an exhibition space but a global business stage,” adding, “I hope it becomes a place where participating companies and visitors can enjoy diverse experiences, connect with one another, and begin creating tangible results.”
